scope: Read-only scientific review of the completed original PAS five-window deployment measurement; acceptance of evidence, not method quality or optimized deployment superiority.
supported: The retained dynamic candidate used 24.8625–26.7985% less peak GPU allocated memory than the original complete PAS implementation on these same-card fixed windows.
limitations: Actual original PAS implementation retains its mixed dtypes, mandatory masks, CPU training-history objects and tiny GPU statistics. This is not an equal-dtype, optimally folded PAS comparison.
Five fixed fresh 32-token windows demonstrate these measured allocated peaks, not the worst peak over all inputs, latency, energy, or total host memory.
This resource-only pass does not improve or newly validate PAS F1, and use of its formal checkpoint for resources is not permission to use it as a FIT-only teacher or quality-selection control.

PAS preparation mistakenly hashed an overbroad historical source map once; the preserved preactivation record reports 12.935504918918014 seconds, no QA parsing, quality consumption or model requests. This is cost, not scientific progress.
No speed advantage is established because this run did not measure latency.
Parameter-byte counts, required masks, ordinary buffers, saved checkpoint bytes, host metadata and runtime peak memory are distinct quantities; none substitutes for another.
The new resource evidence neither changes formal PAS quality nor establishes the candidate aggregate F1 exceeds the strongest baseline.
preparation_disclosure: The preactivation overbroad hash map and its cost are retained in PREACTIVATION_RUNTIME_FILTER.json; the runtime source and scientific protocol were not modified by that filtering.
review_execution: Local JSON reading, small evidence-file SHA binding and arithmetic on verified GPU peak scalars only. No model, remote access, QA parsing, scoring, large checkpoint hash, or source modification.
